title: Protections for LGBTQ+ Youth in Pennsylvania Schools’ Anti-Bullying Policies
content: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ+) youth experience peer victimization at disproportionate rates compared to their heterosexual peers, with poor mental health, substance abuse, and negative academic consequences as associated outcomes. Although federal and state legislation seek to address discrimination and bullying, it remains unclear how these mandates translate to district policies and protect LGBTQ+ students. In the current study, we reviewed school district antibullying policies in Pennsylvania during the 2024–2025 school year to examine overall policy adoption, references to Title IX, and protections for LGBTQ+ youth. Results indicated that 100% of the PA school districts had adopted an antibullying policy and 84.5% directly referenced Title IX; however, only 14 districts (2.8%) specifically outlined protections for LGBTQ+ youth. Chi-square analyses show that school districts that explicitly referenced Title IX in their antibullying policies were less likely to include additional LGBTQ+ protections. Findings suggest that, despite widespread adoption of antibullying policies and frequent references to Title IX, explicit protections for LGBTQ+ youth remain limited in PA school district policies. Because of their enhanced risk for victimization through bullying, school districts should consider including language that directly protects such marginalized groups to safeguard them from harm and victimization.
